pll1d39c3-d1e3501.summary: Reports that some say God can know more than he knows: he can make things that will never be and would know them, and if he made them besides what is, he would know more. Yet his knowledge cannot increase, since this could all happen without change in knowledge.
claims: God could know more things without his knowledge changing.

pll1d39c3-d1e3504.summary: Concludes that God's knowledge is wholly immutable and cannot increase or decrease; only its objects can.
claims: God's knowledge is immutable; its objects vary.

pl-l1d39c3.summary: Reports that some say God can know more than he knows, since he could make things that will never be and would know them. Yet his knowledge cannot increase, since this could happen without change in knowledge. So God's knowledge is wholly immutable; only what is subject to it can increase or decrease.
claims: God could know more things than he does, if he made more.
Only the objects of God's knowledge could vary.
